assumptions: Success rate means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
The period analysed is 1 October 2026 to 31 October 2026, across all regions.
caveats: The success rate depends on the denominator: attempt-level 89.2%, order-level 91.6%, technical 92.9%. Retries and drop-offs explain the gap.
Duplicate records on 12 Oct (341 attempts ingested twice) were removed so each attempt is counted once.
Volume was unusually high from 18 Oct to 31 Oct, so totals should be compared with other periods with care.

facts.text: The attempt-level success rate for 1-31 October 2026 is 89.2%: 384,193 successful attempts out of 430,580 attempts.
Under other definitions the success rate is 91.6% at order level (384,192 of 419,385 orders) and 92.9% technical (384,193 of 413,684). The widest gap between definitions is 3.64pp.
On 12 Oct, 341 attempts were ingested twice (11,704 raw rows vs 11,363 unique attempts). Each attempt is counted once in the figures above.
Attempt volume from 18 Oct to 31 Oct was 39% higher than the usual level for those weekdays, over 14 days.

response.headline: This month (October 2026) the attempt-level payment success rate is 89.2%, with 384,193 successful attempts out of 430,580 total attempts.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Compare retry counts per order and the share of orders that succeeded only after a retry.
hypotheses.rationale: Attempt-level counts every retry as a separate attempt, while order-level counts each order once; the order-level rate is higher (91.6% vs 89.2%).
hypotheses.text: The gap between the attempt-level rate and the order-level rate is likely driven by retries: failed attempts that are later retried successfully count as failures at attempt level but as one success at order level.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check the campaign and sales calendar and confirm ingestion completeness for those dates.
hypotheses.rationale: Volume was 39% above usual weekday levels from 18 Oct to 31 Oct, and both real business events and data gaps look like this.
hypotheses.text: The late-October volume spike may reflect a sale or promotional event rather than a data gap.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: The attempt-level, order-level and technical rates differ, with a maximum gap of 3.64pp.
recommendations.rationale: The rate changes by up to 3.64pp depending on the denominator, which can cause confusion between teams.
recommendations.text: Quote the success rate together with its definition (attempt-level 89.2%) whenever it is shared, and show the order-level rate alongside for context.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: The late-October volume spike may reflect a sale or promotional event rather than a data gap.
recommendations.rationale: A sale or a data gap would affect comparisons differently.
recommendations.text: Check the cause of the 18-31 Oct volume spike before comparing this month's totals with other periods.
